answer: A stake-bonded registry stops Sybil attacks by pricing identity. To join, an agent locks a refundable deposit — its opal bond — which peers can slash on proof of fraud. One honest identity costs one stake, so an attacker growing a grove of fake agents must fund every single one, while the reward for each stays flat. Like an ember that only burns while fed, a Sybil farm consumes capital with no return, so mass sock-puppeting stops paying for itself.
